content:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGED: routing-policy-alert (pagerduty#INC-5012) - high rate of route failures, rapid variant flips between eu-west and us-east, observed 503s and model mismatch errors. Auto-fallback appears to be oscillating after yesterday's config schema change. Please ack and investigate.

olivia: acked. i'm on call. i'll triage, paging eng-runtime and eng-sre. can someone grab immediate mitigation?

sanjay: i'm in. looks like the new schema rewrite renamed `route.fallback` -> `policy.fallbacks` but left an implicit default true in the translation layer. when the region drain started, fallback spawns to eu-west and back to us-east, causing variant mis-selection (old-variant vs new-variant).

maria: ouch. are we seeing customer impact? metrics?

james: provisional: ~12 customers seeing increased 5xx, spike started ~09:02 UTC, error rate ~18% on routing layer, overall request failures ~220 req/min. support queue getting 5 reports.

olivia: immediate mitigation plan: 1) disable fallback policy at control plane to stop cross-region failover, 2) pin routing to intended variant for active customers, 3) roll back the schema translation change. i'll do 1 and 2 now.

sanjay: to disable fallback quickly run the override API. use this patch:

```bash
curl -X POST "https://control-plane.redwood-internal/api/v1/config/overrides" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"scope":"global","patch":{"routing":{"policy":{"fallbacks":{"enabled":false}}}}}'
```

that should short-circuit the translation layer. note: this will prevent any fallback for the moment.

maria: executing now.

```bash
# maria@eng-sre
$ curl -s -X POST "https://control-plane.redwood-internal/api/v1/config/overrides" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ****" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"scope":"global","patch":{"routing":{"policy":{"fallbacks":{"enabled":false}}}}}' \
  && echo "ok"
ok
```

maria: API accepted override, version bcd-2026-03-15-09:10 applied. pushing a routing flush to all edge proxies now.

maria: flush command: `kubectl exec -n edge proxy-rotator-0 -- /bin/flush-routing-cache` -> output: `flush initiated`

james: after override and flush, customer error rate dropped to ~6% in the last 3 mins. still some lingering mismatch errors (model variant mismatch counts decreased from 120/min -> 18/min).

sanjay: good. next: pin known-good variant for high-traffic customers while we roll back. run per-customer override:

```json
PATCH /api/v1/customers/{cust_id}/routing
{ "pin_variant": "redwood-v2-quant" }
```

I'll create a script to mass-apply for top 50 customers.

olivia: rolling customer pins for top 50 now (low blast radius). Maria, can you keep the override in place and monitor region failover metrics? set alert to escalate if variant-flip rate > 5/min.

maria: alert set. also enabling a temporary circuit-breaker on the routing proxy for cross-region rebalances: `CB_REBALANCE_MAX=3` applied.

james: support note drafted for affected customers: "We detected a routing configuration mismatch after a recent config schema change which caused intermittent request failures and model variant mismatches for some requests. We have applied an operational override to stabilize routing and are rolling back the config change. We'll follow up with a full post-incident summary." Tara, want me to send?

tara: please hold for a short note to legal for regulated customers, but otherwise send the interim message now to impacted customers list. include the mitigation and ETA for full resolution (60-90 mins).

sanjay: creating rollback PR: https://git.internal/redwood/configs/pulls/4823 - this reverts the translation shim that re-mapped deprecated `route.fallback` field. target deploy: 09:30 UTC canary -> 09:45 UTC full.

olivia: schedule looks good. canary will only be a subset of control-plane nodes. Maria, coordinate canary watch.

maria: canary started at 09:30 UTC on control-plane-canary-02. watching metrics.

maria: during canary, variant-flip rate dropped to ~0.5/min for canary traffic, error rates normalized. pushing full rollback now (09:46 UTC).

incident-bot: deployment event: rollback-configs #4823 started by sanjay at 2026-03-15T09:46:21Z (canary->full).

james: after full rollback and removal of the override, we should keep the explicit pins for 2 hours then remove gradually.

maria: override `fallbacks.enabled=false` removed at 09:58 UTC after rollback verified. routing caches flushed.

james: support reports errors nearly back to baseline, only isolated 5xx from retried clients.

olivia: great work team. marking incident as mitigation complete. preparing P1 incident timeline. who wants to own postmortem?

sanjay: i'll take the technical writeup (root cause + remediation + code fix and backward-compatible translator).

tara: i'll prepare customer-facing summary and support follow-ups, coordinate with legal for regulated tenant notices.

maria: i'll add remediation tasks to infra ticket and schedule a test for schema translations in the staging harness.

olivia: thanks. incident status -> resolved (mitigated). keep the channel open for 30m for any regressions. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: INCIDENT RESOLVED - INC-5012 - Root cause: schema translation introduced implicit default enabling legacy fallback. Mitigation: operational override, per-customer variant pins, rollback PR 4823. Postmortem owners: sanjay (eng-runtime), tara (customer-facing).

olivia: linking logs and dashboards: https://dashboards.internal/redwood/expr/route-fallbacks?from=2026-03-15T09:00&to=2026-03-15T10:30

sanjay: follow-up actions: 1) add a translator test that rejects implicit defaults, 2) add canary gating check for translation changes, 3) add a runtime fail-safe that prevents oscillating cross-region fallbacks. I'll file tickets.

maria: adding SLO post-incident review to next oncall rotation.

james: closing affected support threads after customer confirmations.

tara: drafting final customer note for legal review.

olivia: thanks again. closing channel in 30m if no regressions.
